- Own supplier performance and time-to-resolution on disruptions mechanisms, driving sourcing strategy to reduce single-points-of-failure on the parts that gate delivery or rate

- Translate strategy into prioritized roadmaps and measurable outcomes, then drive cross-functional decisions when supply, engineering, quality and production priorities conflict

- Build and operationalize an innovation pipeline of supplier pilots, partnerships, and new capabilities that strengthen supply continuity and long-term cost position

- Connect supplier performance and supply risk to unit cost and the integrated master schedule, so supply chain health is visible in program level financial and schedule KPIs

- Define which supply metrics drive decisions versus which report status, building leading indicator systems that enable early intervention

- Leverage quantitative models, including trade studies, sensitivity analysis, and predictive modeling, to inform sourcing strategy and resource allocation

- Prepare analysis, documentation, and briefings for internal teams, suppliers, customers, and government stakeholders

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 6+ years in supply chain strategy, sourcing, or supply program management on complex hardware programs through development and production

- Demonstrated ownership of supply risk and supplier performance on programs with aggressive timelines and rapid scale

- Proven ability to lead cross-functional transformation without direct authority

- Experience building supply chain capabilities or program management systems from scratch in environments without an established playbook

- Ability to translate complex supply and cost data into actionable strategy and clear prioritization

- Comfortable building or interpreting quantitative models to inform sourcing and program decisions

- Familiar with version control, scripting, scalable workflows, and reproducible analysis practices

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated application of structured problem solving and process improvement in production supply chains

- Experience in aerospace, defense, or autonomous systems supply chains

- Track record building and scaling innovation pipelines, supplier pilots, or new sourcing capabilities

- Proficiency with data tools such as Palantir Foundry, discrete event simulation, or custom analytics stacks

- Background in trade studies, causal modeling, or sensitivity analysis applied to supply or production decisions

- Experience interfacing with government customers (DCMA, USAF) on supply status and delivery

We’re building the future of defense manufacturing — and that starts with how we train, develop, and scale our workforce. - Track Outcomes & Drive Improvement: Measure training effectiveness using key operational metrics (e.g., time-to-productivity, picking/packing accuracy, system transaction errors, safety compliance) and use this data to continuously improve programs.

- Must have experience working within or directly supporting a supply chain, warehouse, or materials management function within a fast-paced production or manufacturing environment.

- Experience leading and managing direct reports (this role will have 2 direct reports).

- Demonstrated experience executing, standardizing, and scaling training/onboarding programs across multiple physical locations or sites.

- Superb facilitation and coaching skills—able to engage and train frontline materials handlers, operations managers, and specialized industrial engineers.

- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to lead multiple projects concurrently in a rapidly scaling environment.

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

- Direct experience training staff on ERP and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), specifically Oracle, Forge WMS, and Autotime.

- Experience supporting system migrations and tool adoption training

- Deep understanding of warehouse safety standards, 5S methodologies, inventory control practices (cycle counting, reconciliation), and materials flow engineering.

jobs.title: Senior Finance Director, AD&S
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

We’re looking for a Senior Director to join the finance team supporting Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S), one of Anduril’s largest and fastest-growing divisions. This is a high-visibility financial leadership role responsible for owning the P&L for Anduril’s Autonomous Air Power business line within AD&S. This role is responsible for leading and developing a high-powered team that partners with business to drive product and program profitability.

The successful candidate will operate at both the strategic level — architecting sustainable financial models and shaping the division’s capital allocation — and the operational level — embedding with division and business line leaders to drive day-to-day financial rigor. This role will interface cross-functionally with senior leadership across finance, operations, production, engineering, growth, program management, and supply chain to shape and execute on the business line’s long-term business objectives.

This is a builder’s role — Fury is just the beginning.

ABOUT THE TEAM

AD&S is fundamentally reshaping the way future peer to peer conflicts are fought by developing next generation collaborative combat aircraft (like our unmanned fighter jet Fury), advanced effects (like our air-breathing cruise missile Barracuda), and the autonomy software that powers these weapons. The team is responsible for taking products from initial concept to full-rate production at-scale. The team also develops Lattice for Mission Autonomy, Anduril’s premier software platform that enables masses of Fury, Barracuda, and other robots to collaborate across various missions and environments. Our autonomous systems are the cornerstone of these capabilities, and we continually strive to push the boundaries of the possible in terms of range, autonomy, and mission capability.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

- Daily partnership with Senior Leaders within AD&S to bring first class financial expertise and support to the business.

- Manage the processes for financial forecasting and budgets, and oversee the preparation of business line, product and program level financial reporting.

- Own the financial oversight and management for a portfolio of large, complex, and mission-critical programs

- Manage and scale a dedicated team in line with the needs of the business by developing and hiring best-in-class talent and implementing best practices and tools to ensure a well-controlled yet flexible finance organization.

- Lead the development of executive-level reporting and present financial insights to senior management.

- Evaluate financial performance by comparing and analyzing actual results with forecasts, highlighting trends and analyzing causes of unexpected variances.

- Work with senior AD&S and corporate finance leaders to identify and implement ways to improve business performance and finance systems, tools and processes.

- Get deep in the operations and support the team in creating bottoms-up, data-driven models to understand segmentation, pricing optimization, scenarios, and financial returns of our products and investments.

- Own performance dashboards, alerting, and investigation into KPI health. Assess the impact of financial decisions on KPIs while developing strategies which drive demonstrable impact against these metrics.

- Develop deep relationships with our customers (both internal and external) and oversee customer program reporting, monthly invoicing, and monthly financial status reporting.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

In Materials Management, you will be joining the new home for Special Projects in one of Anduril’s largest, most critical functions.  As a Senior Materials Program Manager, you will tackle high-priority initiatives to scale our physical footprint, streamline material flow, and safeguard high-value inventory. We are looking for a heavy-hitter with deep supply chain knowledge who can operate autonomously, lead cross-functional projects, and ensure our materials infrastructure enables production to deliver hardware On-time, with Quality, and at Cost.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
You will lead some of the most consequential strategic work at the company — building the analytical foundation and forward-looking strategy that de-risks our Supply Chain as we scale production across a growing portfolio of products. You will partner directly with executives across Supply Chain to translate ambiguous, high-stakes problems into structured analyses and executable strategies.

- Drive Material Management Strategy: Develop a deep, first-principles understanding of material management and flow, sub-tier suppliers, and geopolitical dynamics that drive risk in our supply chain. Build analytics to size exposure, monitor leading indicators, and inform investment decisions on inventory, material flow, ERP/WMS integration, and federal compliance.

- Build the Strategy, Then Drive It: Synthesize analyses into a coherent material management strategy and bring it to life through executive recommendations. Own work end-to-end — from problem definition, to quantitative modeling, to exec-ready synthesis, to cross-functional implementation.

- Collaborate with Executives: Structure and lead working sessions with senior leaders to frame decisions and drive alignment on trade-offs that materially shape the cost, schedule, and resilience of our production base. Translate complex findings into crisp narratives enabling rapid decision-making.

- Go Deep in Data and Systems: Master our ERP, MRP, and supply chain data. Build scrappy analyses on short timelines and develop tooling / dashboards that let functional teams continuously measure and act on critical metrics.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- You have 5+ years of experience in manufacturing or supply chain operations, management consulting - or some other experience where you just had to figure out how to get stuff done.

- Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- You are self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don’t need someone to tell you to “move”. You just move. We’d rather have to tell you to slow down than to speed up.

- You don’t wait on others to solve problems. You proactively step into the gap to offer solutions yourself.

- You don’t have to be told what to do or how to do it - you’re the first one to bring forward solutions and ideas, and then receptively take feedback on them and iterate with the team. You enjoy the idea of seeing your team as “guardrails” to keep you on track, but not the engine pushing you forward. You are that engine!

- You have an appetite to build clear frameworks to structure problems. Hardware startups are messy - bringing clarity and structured-thinking to the table is a huge asset.

- You lean into acknowledging your weaknesses and take the idea of feedback and growth seriously.

- You get energy from being a thought partner for others and it excites you to spend time translating operational problems into data problems, and to then going and executing on them.

- You enjoy working at a place where no one minds if you leave early one day to go to an appointment or run an errand, but you also don’t mind responding to Slacks in the evening while you’re watching Netflix.

- You have an appetite to build clear frameworks to structure problems.

- You have strong analytical aptitude. You intuitively think about problems in terms of numbers and data-models, and you are able to quickly execute analyses in Excel or other tools.

- You are comfortable communicating broadly and having a lot of eyes on your work. This role can at-times require comms to large groups and senior leadership. This should excite you!

- Identify and mitigate potential risks and issues that may impact program delivery.

- Continuously seek opportunities for process improvement and efficiency within the program.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built, and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

The M&A Business Systems team is the tip of the spear when Anduril acquires a new company. We are a small, fast-moving team responsible for integrating acquired companies into Anduril's Oracle Fusion ERP and best in class internal tools. We operate an aggressive acquisition roadmap and run multiple integration programs in parallel at any given time, enabling operations across the U.S. and internationally.

The Role

We are seeking an early career, quick to learn Solution Analyst, M&A to join the M&A Business Systems team and own hands-on configuration, data manipulation, and integration work across our full acquisition portfolio. A successful Solution Analyst will own much of the configuration and data work related to M&A. They will also be expected to grow their skillset by being embedded in the full integration lifecycle from the moment a deal closes: involved in onsite discovery, providing fit/gap analyses, completing build/configuration, converting data, executing test scenarios, and supporting Go-Lives at acquired sites. You'll be the person who ensures a newly acquired company can actually operate from day one inside Anduril's enterprise systems across all work streams.

You will work directly with the broader M&A systems team, collaborating across EngOS/PLM (Teamcenter), home-grown manufacturing and planning systems (Forge, MRPSpeed), customer and contract mgmt (Salesforce), and the Oracle Fusion ERP core spanning procurement, inventory, order management and finance/accounting. If you thrive in high-tempo, ambiguous environments where the answer isn't in a playbook yet and you have the scars to prove you've been here before, this role was written for you.

Key Responsibilities

- Own end-to-end data conversion for M&A integrations: extract source data, map to Oracle templates, derive business rules for undefined fields, validate data quality and leverage AI tools to eliminate manual work and build repeatable processes for future acquisitions

- Support legal entity design and intercompany configuration for new acquisitions, translating operational, accounting and legal requirements into application design decisions for ERP and satellite system teams.

- Execute system configuration for new Oracle legal entities across workstreams: DTB (Design to Build), WMS (Warehouse/Inventory Operations), PTP (Procure to Pay), OTC (Order to Cash), PTC (Projects to Close), and RTR (Record to Report).

- Plan and execute testing cycles, build and run test cases, resolve defects, and drive root cause and resolution with satellite system teams (Teamcenter, Forge, Salesforce, MRPSpeed).

- Travel onsite to acquired companies to lead discovery sessions, demos, deliver hands-on ERP training, and provide Go-Live and Hypercare support.

- Collaborate with the M&A PM and enablement functions to build and maintain standardized data templates, integration SOPs, and reusable training materials (videos, guides) that scale the team's playbook across future acquisitions.

- Partner with cross-functional satellite tool teams (PLM/Teamcenter, Forge/MES, Salesforce, WMS) to coordinate configuration changes and test dependencies on acquisition timelines.

- Operate in agile/sprint-based delivery: own your workstream, hit sprint milestones, surface blockers early, and keep integration programs moving without being told what to do next.

- Contribute to and maintain the M&A ERP knowledge base, capture design decisions, configuration documentation, and lessons learned in Airtable and Quip so future integrations start further ahead.

Required Characteristics

Anduril is an extremely fast-paced defense technology company. The M&A team runs at a pace most teams don't. The successful candidate will demonstrate:

- Bias for Action — you move fast, escalate blockers immediately, and don't wait for perfect information to make progress.

- Outcome-Oriented — you care about Day 1 Go-live working, not about process elegance. You work backward from the deadline.

- Ownership — you own your workstream end to end. If something is at risk, you raise it and you fix it.

- Agility — acquisition timelines shift. Legal entity decisions get made late. You adapt without drama.

- Dive Deep — you're comfortable in the weeds of data templates, config workbooks, and test scripts. You spot the gap before it becomes a blocker.

- Customer Focus — you treat acquired company employees as your users. You build trust with teams who are often new to enterprise systems and nervous about change.

- First Principles Thinking — you don't just replicate how the last integration was done. You ask whether it was the right way and improve the playbook.

Required Qualifications

- 3+ years of hands-on ERP experience (Oracle Fusion preferred but will accept NetSuite, SAP, or similar), including configuration, data conversion/loading, and troubleshooting — M&A integration or rapid deployment experience strongly preferred.

- Demonstrated experience executing data migrations: extracting source data, mapping to target templates, validating quality, and coordinating loads.

- Deep knowledge in at least one or more particular work streams (order to cash, procure to pay, record to report, design to build, etc.) strongly preferred

- Strong understanding of legal entity and intercompany transaction design — experience configuring new legal entities in Oracle Fusion is a significant plus.

- Proven ability to work in agile/sprint-based delivery environments; comfortable writing user stories, tracking work in PM tools (Airtable, Jira, or equivalent), and iterating quickly.

- Strong cross-functional communication skills — you can work with accounting, legal, ops, engineers, and ERP developers in the same day and adjust your communication style for each.

- Willingness and ability to travel up to 50% , including to acquired company sites domestically and internationally, for discovery, onboarding, testing, and Go-live support.

- U.S. Person status required (access to export-controlled data).

- Ability to work onsite full-time at primary office location.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with M&A ERP integration programs or ERP rapid deployment / accelerated implementation methodologies.

- Familiarity with connected enterprise tools: Teamcenter/PLM, Salesforce, Odoo, or similar.

- Prior experience at Big 4 consulting firms in ERP implementation practices.

- Aerospace & Defense, complex manufacturing, or government contracting industry background.

- Experience building reusable enablement content — training videos, SOPs, how-to guides — for end users who are new to ERP systems.

- Undergraduate degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Supply Chain, or related field.

$86,000 — $114,000 USD

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Maritime delivers platforms, systems, and integrated effects in the maritime domain. Our autonomous vehicles (sub-surface and surface) are the cornerstone of these capabilities, and we continually strive to push the boundaries of the possible in terms of endurance, autonomy and mission capability. The Maritime team develops and maintains core products and payloads and adapts and applies those products to serve a wide variety of defense, IC and commercial customers in US and international markets.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Director, Maritime Business Development (Strategy) to join our team to shape, capture, and grow new maritime concepts, products and future business lines. This is a zero-to-one role. You will partner with engineering, product, and division leadership to define the customer set, translate customer mission requirements into a credible product strategy, build the partnerships required to deliver the capability, and lead the captures that turn the concept into a program of record.

Success in this role requires comfort operating at the intersection of strategy and emerging technology — you will need to be conversant in the technical reality of what makes these systems work, the operational reality of how customers will use them, and the programmatic reality of how the U.S. government and commercial customers acquire first-of-kind capability. The role asks for a leader who is energized by greenfield problems and is willing to roll up their sleeves and build a capability and program from scratch.

If you have spent time in consulting, defense business development, commercial maritime, government program acquisitions, defense strategy, or the intersection of advanced technology and national security, and you are looking for a role where the strategy, customer relationships and the technical shaping all sit in the same seat, this is the role for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Originate and shape business opportunities.  You will own the front end of the pipeline for the Maritime Division: identifying where the next programs and markets will form, then building the engagement strategy to get there first. You will develop a deep, current view of the client base, the programmatic and technical roadmap, and a shifting competitive landscape, and translate that view into a deliberate set of pursuits. You will initiate and sustain executive-level engagements with existing and prospective customers, read buying cycles before they open, and lead the response strategy for RFIs, RFPs, RFWPs, and unsolicited proposals that position Anduril to win.

- Own the growth strategy.  Build and execute a cohesive, data-driven strategy to shape, capture, and close emerging growth opportunities in new or existing markets that allow the Maritime Division to penetrate, expand, and deliver Anduril's best-in-class warfighting capabilities to defense and commercial customers.

- Stand up new programs from scratch.  Lead the rapid shaping, capture, design, and prototyping of new commercial and defense products where a program or market has to be grown from scratch or from early requirements, partnering with Government Relations, Marketing, and Communications to bring it to life.

- Expand into adjacent demand.  You will work alongside other business lines and product engineers to find new growth inside existing accounts: not just scaling current programs, but using established client relationships as a wedge into new mission areas and budget lines they have not yet opened to us. You will turn trusted access into new program starts.

- Shape the market narrative.  You represent Anduril to clients, partners, competitors, and the public, but the goal is more than communication: you will frame the problems, concepts of operation, and requirements that move customers toward the capabilities we build. You will use insight and a clear point of view to educate the market and create demand where a category does not yet exist.

- Define what we build next.  You will sit between emerging customer problems and the engineering organization, translating early, ill-defined needs into a concrete product thesis and roadmap. You will decide which signals are real, convert them into requirements engineering can act on, align internal priorities and stakeholders behind them, and hold the new effort to its key milestones.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- The ideal candidate will be a proven development and growth leader with prior experience in commercial or DoD Capture and Sales, demonstrating a track record of shaping a capability from concept through funded prototyping or program of record start, particularly with an emphasis on the US Navy as a customer.

- Demonstrated knowledge of defense acquisition, including a track record of zero-to-one program growth: taking a capability from concept or early requirements through funded start.

- Prior experience developing emerging concepts into tangible strategies and pursuits for 2027 and beyond

- Familiarity with the full product lifecycle, from concept and prototyping through fielding and sustainment, and the ability to work across engineering, capture, and operations to move a new effort through it.

- Demonstrated high-energy, high-ownership leader who will drive performance and exhibit strong management skills with a high level of emotional intelligence. About the Role

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain to build and lead the supply chain function at Arsenal-1, our flagship factory in the Columbus, Ohio area. Starting from a blank sheet, you will make sure material, capacity, and supplier readiness are in place ahead of every rate increase and every new product family that lands on the floor.
Reporting to the Senior Director of Manufacturing Operations, you will set the multi-year strategy for how the function evolves, spanning org design, process architecture, systems roadmap, and talent, while staying close enough to the work to personally unblock the hardest constraints and represent supply chain credibly to executive leadership.
This is not a role where you delegate and observe. You will be in the details on the highest-stakes shortages and escalations while building an organization that can increasingly handle them without you. If you are energized by building a function that becomes a durable competitive advantage, and by developing the leaders who will run it, this is the role.

What You'll Do

Stand Up the Arsenal-1 Supply Chain Function

- Define the charter and scope of the Arsenal-1 supply chain function: what the site owns, what the broader Supply Chain team owns, and how the overlap between them is governed.

- Build the integrated plan for standing up the function: phased by production milestone, with entry and exit criteria, named owners, and hard dates. Work backward from production start and each rate step to define required readiness in people, process, systems, supplier qualification, and inventory position.

- Own the risk register, dependency map, and critical path, along with the governance around them: readiness and gate reviews, plus an executive cadence that gives leadership real status without generating theater.

- Write the operating model: planning cadences, material call and shortage escalation, receiving and inspection flow, kitting and line-feed, cycle counting, change control, and decision rights for each.

- Own the capital, tooling, and infrastructure requests supply chain depends on (storage footprint, material handling, receiving and inspection capacity), sequenced against facility construction.

Drive Material and Supplier Readiness

- Drive supplier readiness with Sourcing, Product Sourcing Engineering, and Supplier Quality: qualification, capacity reservation, tooling, and dual-source coverage completed ahead of need dates, not in parallel with production.

- Own the readiness sequence for manufacturing BOM release, including BOM risk assessment and alternate component strategy for constrained and long-lead parts.

- Define and drive the metrics that matter: clear-to-build, material availability, schedule attainment, supplier on-time delivery, and inventory accuracy. Hold the team to root-causing misses rather than expediting around them.

- Serve as the senior supply chain voice at the site. Own executive relationships across Sourcing, Manufacturing, Engineering, Finance, and Deployment Ops, and translate material shortages, capacity limits, and supplier risk into clear recommendations for leadership and stakeholders.

Turn the Startup into a Day-to-Day Operation

- Convert the standup effort into a durable operating function — replace one-off heroics and manual workarounds with standard cadences, documented processes, and clear decision rights that run without you in the room.

- Build and scale the team as headcount ramps: hire and develop planners, buyers, and material leaders; design the org structure the site grows into; and create a culture that retains strong operators.

- Mature the systems backbone so the function runs on reliable data rather than spreadsheets — stand up and stabilize ERP/MRP and planning tooling as volume and product mix grow.

- Institutionalize continuous improvement: establish the metrics, reviews, and root-cause discipline that let the function keep pace with each rate increase and every new product family, and shift the team from firefighting to steady-state execution.

How This Role Works with the Central Supply Chain Team

Anduril is building a central Supply Chain organization, led by the VP of Supply Chain, that sets the strategy, standards, and best practices every site runs on. This role is the primary Arsenal-1 counterpart to that team — the site liaison who translates enterprise supply chain strategy into execution on our floor and carries the site's realities back the other way.

- Governance and standards: you adopt and localize the enterprise operating model — planning and S&OP standards, supplier and sourcing strategy, ERP/MRP configuration and data conventions, and KPI definitions — so Arsenal-1 stays consistent with the broader network.

- Site autonomy: you own the day-to-day execution and site-level decisions — planning cadences, material calls and shortage priorities, inventory positioning, local buyer and supplier relationships, and hiring at the site.

- Two-way flow: you carry Arsenal-1's needs and lessons learned back into enterprise strategy, and you hold a dotted-line relationship to the VP of Supply Chain for central guidance, standardization, and network-wide alignment — while reporting solid-line to Manufacturing Operations at the site.

Required Qualifications

- 10+ years in supply chain, materials management, planning, or manufacturing operations in a hardware or manufacturing environment, including 5+ years managing people and at least 2 years managing managers or leading a multi-team function.

- You've built and scaled an organization, not just a team: hiring senior talent, developing managers, designing structure, and creating a culture that retains strong operators.

- You've owned S&OP or an equivalent enterprise planning process end to end, with real accountability for material availability and schedule attainment.

- You think in systems and have deep operational instincts. You understand how upstream decisions in engineering, product, and sourcing cascade into downstream materials, manufacturing, and fulfillment outcomes. You can decompose an ambiguous, high-stakes supply problem and drive it to resolution fast.

- You're data-driven and systems-fluent across ERP/MRP platforms (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Oracle) and advanced planning tools, and you can partner credibly with technical teams to improve tooling — while knowing when a spreadsheet is the right answer.

- Strong executive presence, high ownership, low ego. You align senior stakeholders, communicate trade-offs crisply, hold your ground with data, and value results over credit.

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or a related field, and the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience leading supply chain in a high-growth hardware, aerospace, or defense environment.

- Experience scaling from low-rate to high-rate production, including capacity and footprint planning.

- Track record of standing up or rebuilding a supply chain function and its supporting systems from the ground up.

- Experience with a multi-product portfolio with shared supply and constrained long-lead materials.

- Familiarity with defense program environments and contract-driven delivery commitments.

- MBA or advanced degree in a relevant field.

As the lead for your assigned mineral, you will own the global mandate end-to-end: market intelligence, tiered supply chain mapping, supplier and government relationship management, should-cost modeling, contracting, and stockpiling strategy. You will operate as the hub of a cross-functional pod to translate Anduril's aggregate demand into a resilient sourcing strategy that enhances supplies from US-friendly sources, protects BOM cost, and ensures continuity of supply across NPI and mass production.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Strategy & Visibility

- Own the commodity strategy for your assigned critical mineral, with explicit focus on supply chain resilience, geopolitical risk mitigation (particularly PRC concentration in mining and refinement), cost, and quality

- Build and maintain tiered supply chain mapping from Anduril end products down to the raw material, quantify revenue exposure and BOM impact to prioritize where deeper intervention is needed

- Market Intelligence & Comms

- Maintain expert-level market intelligence and deliver weekly updates on pricing, disruptions, and geopolitical signals

- Host monthly cross-functional pod tag-ups, lead quarterly strategy reviews, and conduct regular executive briefings on market conditions and mitigation plans

- Sourcing Execution

- Lead RFI/RFQ/RFP processes across miners, refiners, processors, and component suppliers

- Perform should-cost and TCO analysis; negotiate key agreements (offtake, pricing, capacity reservations, payment terms) suited to volatile, concentrated markets

- Evaluate and recommend strategic interventions (stockpiling, prepayments, JVs, equity investments, vertical integration), partnering with CorpDev and Finance

- Relationship Management

- Build trusted relationships with suppliers, industry associations, and U.S./allied government bodies (DoD, DPA Title III, DLA, DOE); represent Anduril externally for your commodity

- Cross-Functional Leadership

- Lead a cross-functional pod spanning product sourcing, parent commodity managers, Engineering, and CorpDev/Finance

- Partner with Engineering to qualify alternates, influence specs, and design out single points of failure

- Supplier & Performance Management

- Own supplier performance (delivery, quality, cost, innovation), serving as primary escalation point and managing continuity of supply through NPI-to-MP transitions

You’ll dive into a fast-paced environment, partnering with multidisciplinary teams to design, scale, and secure robust, high-performance global supply chains. We're seeking talented Sourcing professionals with deep expertise in supplier negotiation, category management, and strategic partnership development to help build the next generation of defense technology.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the Category Strategy: Develop and execute end-to-end sourcing strategies across your assigned category, balancing cost, quality, lead time, capacity, and supply security to meet aggressive program timelines.

- Build the Supplier Base: Identify, qualify, and onboard best-in-class domestic and international suppliers. Own the relationship through QBRs, scorecards, capacity planning, and continuous performance management.

- Lead Commercial Negotiations: Structure and negotiate complex supplier agreements — MSAs, SOWs, LTAs, pricing agreements, and NRE terms — to lock in favorable commercial terms and de-risk supply.

- Partner Cross-Functionally: Embed with Engineering, Quality, and Manufacturing during NPI to align design intent with supplier capability, drive design-to-cost, and get parts qualified and flowing on schedule.

- De-Risk the Supply Chain: Track market dynamics, geopolitics, and upstream constraints. Identify single points of failure and stand up dual-source, buffer, or vertical-integration strategies before they become production stoppages.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or a related field, with 10+ years in global sourcing, strategic procurement, or supplier management inside a high-tech or regulated manufacturing environment.

- Commercial Depth: Working command of commercial contract law, should-cost modeling, and a track record of closing high-value, technically complex agreements.

- Category & Supply Base Management: Demonstrated success managing a global supplier base, running audits, and scaling supply from prototype through high-rate production.

- Technical Fluency: Comfortable reading engineering drawings and specs, and translating cleanly between engineers and supplier commercial/technical counterparts.

- Clearance: Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

The Business Development Recruiting team is responsible for attracting and hiring the talent that builds Anduril's growth engine. As Anduril scales into new markets, new programs of record, and new customer sets, these functions grow in complexity and criticality — and the quality of the people we bring in directly shapes how the company identifies, wins, and expands its most consequential opportunities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Recruiter for Business Development to join our rapidly growing team in Washington, DC (preferred), Costa Mesa, CA, Seattle, WA, or Boston, MA office.

In this role, you will own full-cycle recruiting across Business Development, Government Relations, and Program Management, while providing flex support to adjacent Growth searches as needed. You will build deep partnerships with your hiring managers, becoming a trusted extension of their teams, while developing real relationships with candidates throughout the process. This will require the versatility to context-switch across searches that demand very different domain fluency, candidate pools, and assessment approaches. In a given week you might be sourcing a Capture Manager with PEO experience, screening a Director of Business Development - Air Force for our Air Dominance & Strike Division and closing a Senior Proposal Manager who has run $500M+ competitive bids. You will need to learn each sub-function well enough to credibly evaluate candidates and advise hiring managers on talent strategy, market dynamics, and role design. If you are someone who thrives on variety, closes with precision, and earns trust from both hiring managers and candidates through the quality of your work, this role is for you.

Full-Cycle Recruiting Execution

- Own end-to-end recruiting across Business Development, Government Relations, and Program Management, with flex capacity into adjacent Growth hiring during peak periods

- Develop and execute sourcing strategies tailored to each sub-function, recognizing that a capture manager pipeline rooted in the DoD acquisition community looks very different from a government relations pipeline built around former Hill staff and agency liaisons

- Conduct screens that assess functional depth, customer knowledge, and organizational fit, with an evaluation approach calibrated to each search — a capture lead requires different proof points than a proposal manager or a BD representative

- Manage the interview process from intake through close: calibrate with hiring managers, prepare interview panels, facilitate debriefs, and drive offers to signature

Strategic Partnership

- Partner with BD and Growth leaders to understand current and upcoming hiring needs, team composition, and the specific profiles that will succeed in each sub-function and division

- Provide transparent pipeline updates and market intelligence, especially when conditions require recalibrating timelines, expectations, or clearance assumptions

- Influence role design and leveling by bringing external market perspective to internal conversations about scope, customer alignment, and requirements

- Own the candidate experience from first outreach through close, making sure every interaction reflects the credibility and mission-seriousness that senior BD candidates expect

- Maintain data integrity in the ATS/CRM to support accurate reporting, capacity planning, and pipeline analytics

- Identify and implement improvements to recruiting processes, tools, and interview practices within your portfolio

- Collaborate with the broader Talent Acquisition team to share market intelligence, sourcing strategies, and best practices across the Growth and BD recruiting functions

- 5–8+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

- Direct experience recruiting within business development, capture, proposals, government relations, program management, or adjacent growth functions — ideally in defense, aerospace, or national security

- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent searches across different functional areas while maintaining quality and candidate experience

- Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to advise, calibrate, and build trust with hiring managers across levels

- Data-informed mindset: you track pipeline metrics, use conversion data to diagnose search health, and present market intelligence to influence decisions

- Clear, effective communication with candidates and hiring teams, with the ability to build rapport and assess fit across a range of BD disciplines

- Ability to move fast and prioritize without letting quality or candidate experience slip

- Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience recruiting in defense, aerospace, or a related industry where cleared talent, customer relationships, and program knowledge are central to candidate evaluation

- Familiarity with the DoD acquisition ecosystem — you understand what a PEO does, how capture campaigns work, and why a candidate's program history matters

- Experience recruiting across multiple BD sub-functions rather than a single specialty (e.g., both capture and government relations, not just one)

- Track record of improving recruiting processes, interview design, or assessment frameworks

- Working knowledge of security clearance processes and how clearance status affects pipeline timelines and offer strategy

- Established network or sourcing muscle in the defense BD talent market, including candidates moving between primes, non-traditional defense companies, and government service

The Supply Chain Project Manager is a hands-on builder and problem-solver within the Supply Chain PMO who designs, develops, and deploys new processes and systems across the organization. This role requires someone who can take ambiguous supply chain challenges—whether in sourcing, cost management, new product introduction, or manufacturing—and partner with subject matter experts to architect scalable process solutions from the ground up. You'll own complete work streams from discovery through implementation—conducting stakeholder interviews, mapping current-state workflows, designing future-state processes, and leading the deployment and change management efforts. The Supply Chain Project Manager collaborates closely with Program Managers and cross-functional partners (like Engineering, IT, Procurement, and Manufacturing) to transform operational needs into documented, repeatable processes that drive organizational efficiency and effectiveness.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Own end-to-end process development for key supply chain initiatives—from eliciting vague requirements to delivering fully documented, deployed, and adopted processes.

- Conduct discovery and requirements gathering by interviewing subject matter experts, facilitating workshops, and synthesizing complex information into clear problem statements and solution approaches.

- Design and document new business processes, including workflow diagrams, standard operating procedures, RACI matrices, process narratives, and implementation playbooks.

- Lead process deployment and change management efforts, including stakeholder communication, training development and delivery, adoption tracking, and post-implementation refinement.

- Map and analyze current-state processes to identify gaps, bottlenecks, and opportunities for standardization, efficiency gains, and risk reduction.

- Develop process governance frameworks, including success metrics, monitoring approaches, and continuous improvement mechanisms to ensure long-term sustainability.

- Partner with cross-functional teams to define requirements, validate solutions, and ensure new processes integrate seamlessly with existing systems and workflows.

- Facilitate alignment across stakeholder groups, managing competing priorities and building consensus around process standards and implementation approaches.

- Create scalable process templates and frameworks that can be replicated across different teams, programs, or product lines.

- Support program managers by managing specific workstreams within larger transformation initiatives, providing regular status updates and proactively identifying risks.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, industrial engineering, business, or related field.

- 2+ years of progressive experience in material cost management, New Product Introduction (NPI), process design, business process improvement, or program management within the aerospace, defense, or related manufacturing industry.

- Demonstrated ability to design and implement new processes from concept through deployment.

- Experience with change management principles and driving process adoption across organizations.

- Strong facilitation and requirements gathering skills, with the ability to work with ambiguous problems and diverse stakeholders.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- Master's degree in supply chain management, industrial engineering, or related field.

- Certification in process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) or change management (Prosci, ADKAR).

- Experience with business process modeling tools and notation (BPMN, Visio, Lucidchart, Miro).

- Knowledge of program and project management frameworks (PMI, Agile, or similar).

- Deep understanding of supply chain operations including planning, procurement, logistics, and their interdependencies.

- Proven track record of leading organizational change initiatives and achieving measurable adoption and results.

- Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels and build compelling cases for process changes.

- Experience working with ERP systems and understanding how processes translate into system requirements and configurations.

- Ability to work independently in ambiguous situations while knowing when to collaborate and escalate.

- Strong project management skills with ability to manage multiple concurrent work streams.
